title: Privacy, PII & Data Minimization
interviewAnswer: I minimize sensitive data, define purpose and retention, restrict access, encrypt data in transit/at rest, and avoid sending PII to models or logs unless explicitly required and governed. Privacy starts in architecture, not with masking at the end.
why: LLM/ML systems often duplicate data into prompts, vector stores, logs, caches and training sets, multiplying exposure.
intuition: Every extra copy of sensitive data is another place that can leak. Keep only what the system genuinely needs.
deepDive: Redaction/tokenization, tenant isolation, access control, deletion workflows and data lineage are common controls. Embeddings can still reveal information; they should not automatically be treated as anonymized.
workedExample: An internal RAG assistant should enforce document ACLs before retrieval, not retrieve everything and merely ask the LLM not to reveal it.
commonMistakes: Assuming embeddings cannot contain sensitive information.
Logging complete prompts/responses in production by default.
followUps: How do you implement right-to-delete in a vector store?
Where can PII leak in an LLM pipeline?
production: Build classification/retention into ingestion, retrieval, logging and backup policies; test cross-tenant access explicitly.
